html:
The Krivichs were a large union of early East Slavic tribes, living from about the 500s to the 1100s around the upper Dnieper, Western Dvina and upper Volga. On the map for 700 they cover a wide area of today's western Russia and Belarus.

They seem to have started near Pskov and spread into lands where Finnic peoples already lived. Their main towns were Smolensk, Polotsk and Izborsk, and later Pskov. The Primary Chronicle names them with the Slovenes and the Chuds among the peoples who invited the Varangian Rurik to rule them. Their lands lay along the route from the Varangians to the Greeks. They became part of Kievan Rus', and the Principality of Polotsk grew out of their country. In Latvian the word for Russian, krievs, comes from their name.
